stages.journal: Nesh-Deeka gave me the Veiled Reed's first work. Dives-Without-A-Rope, one of the broker's gang, carried off a jar of sap that the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. Nesh-Deeka wants it to learn what the cutters wanted. I'm to ask Dives-Without-A-Rope for the jar in the ship's hold at the pier west of Lilmoth.
Dives-Without-A-Rope is dead. Her lockbox is at the far side of the ship's hold, and the key is on her body. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.

Dives-Without-A-Rope will not give up the jar. It is sap of her own tree, and she keeps it in her lockbox at the far side of the ship's hold, with the key on her. I'm to take the jar by picking the lock or by taking her key, and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.

I talked Dives-Without-A-Rope round. She gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. She asked me in return to find who cut her tree. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
I paid Dives-Without-A-Rope twenty gold. She gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.

I tasted the cutters' sap in Salts-The-Catch's house. Nesh-Deeka wrote down what I said under it: a ship's hold with roots through its deck, a door that was never built, a dry voice. She gave me the page and twenty-five gold. She has heard that the Hist of Low-Reed Village, east of Lilmoth, has turned its face.
Nesh-Deeka is dead. I will not learn from her what the cutters wanted with the jar.

lines.speaker: npc.nesh-deeka
lines.prompt: What does the Reed want of me?
lines.text: I want the cutters' jar, the one Dives-Without-A-Rope carried off the camp. I mean to learn from it what the cutters wanted. It is in the hold of the ship of Buys-The-Months, at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth. Go west along the shore, a fair way, past the old lighthouse. Dives-Without-A-Rope keeps it in the hold. How you get it is your affair. Look over the hold before you decide. Then bring the jar to me here.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: Nesh-Deeka wants the jar you carried off the camp.
lines.text: No. That jar holds sap of Nine Bends, my own tree. It is not for Nesh-Deeka to take. If you lick the sap, the Hist shows you a vision. I mean to lick it and hear my tree once, before anyone takes it from me. The jar is locked in my lockbox on the far side of the hold. I keep the key on me. So what are you to me? A reason, a price or a fight?

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: What did you see at the cutting?
lines.text: I saw them come ashore at night. They were the cutters, the people who cut a Hist's roots. Each carried empty jars. They went straight to the roots of the camp's cutting, the slip of the Hist that grew there. They cut the roots and filled the jars from the cuts. They were quick and quiet. One jar rolled away by the fire. I took it before I thought. I knew it was Nine Bends the moment I held it.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: (Persuade) The one I work for means to find who cut your tree. We can learn it from the jar.
lines.text: You speak as if you mean it. I wanted one taste of my tree before the jar was taken from me. I wanted it badly. But I want more to know who cut Nine Bends. Find who did it. That is all I ask of you. Here is the key. The jar is in my lockbox, on the far side of the hold. I go back to my months with empty hands. Do not make me sorry.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: (Persuade) The one I work for means to find who cut your tree. We can learn it from the jar.
lines.text: You speak as if you mean it. I wanted one taste of my tree before the jar was taken from me. I wanted it badly. But I want more to know who cut Nine Bends. Find who did it. lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: I will give you twenty gold for the key. (20 gold)
lines.text: Twenty gold is a month off my roll, so I will take it. It is not a fair price for Nine Bends. It is what I can spare. Here is the key. My lockbox is on the far side of the hold, and the jar is inside it. Do not tell me what you will do with it. I would rather not hear.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: I will give you twenty gold for the key. (20 gold)
lines.text: Twenty gold is a month off my roll, so I will take it. It is not a fair price for Nine Bends. It is what I can spare. Here is the key. My lockbox is on the far side of the hold, and the jar is inside it. Do not tell me what you will do with it. I would rather not hear.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: What will you do without the jar?
lines.text: I will work off my months as before. I have a shift, my food and my sleep, and that will not change. I meant to taste Nine Bends once. If the jar leaves my hands, I will go without, as I have done for years. I hope whoever has it finds who cut my tree.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-barge.npc-opening-overseer
lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: I am Wuleen-Sei, the broker's overseer in this hold. The gang answers to me, and I answer to Buys-The-Months. Since the camp, my gang will not touch Dives-Without-A-Rope's lockbox. I will not make them. The gang has lost enough. Ask Dives-Without-A-Rope what she keeps in it.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-barge.npc-opening-roll-reader
lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: I am Ux-Xeek, the broker's port hand. I call the gang out to the lighters, the flat boats that carry cargo to the ships, and they must be there on time. The lockpicks on the floor by Dives-Without-A-Rope's lockbox are mine. They are my spares for the lighters' padlocks. I have not counted them today. Now I have work to do.

lines.speaker: npc.nesh-deeka
lines.prompt: Here is the jar Dives-Without-A-Rope carried off the camp.
lines.text: That is the jar. Let me draw the stopper. The sap is fresh from the roots. It was drawn into a jar that the cutters brought with them, so they mean to keep it. This is a long work, not a raid. Whoever tastes Hist sap sees a vision. A stranger may see something else. I do not know which you are. I will write while you put one drop on your tongue. Will you taste it?

lines.speaker: npc.nesh-deeka
lines.prompt: (Alchemy) Let me read the sap first, as a tester does, then taste it.
lines.text: You read it as a tester does. Good. It is fresh sap, drawn from cut roots. The stopper and the neck of the jar show the marks of other jars filled beside it. I will note that. Then you tasted, and I wrote what you said while you were under it. A ship's hold with roots through its deck. A door that was never built, and a voice, dry, that made no words. I cannot tell you what it means, and I will not guess. Keep the page and twenty-five gold, and I will keep the jar. We pay our hands. One more thing, because you are one of mine now: the Hist at Low-Reed, a village east of here, has turned its face from its people.

lines.text: Good. Be still. I will write while you are under it. A ship's hold. Roots through the deck. A door that was never built. A dry voice with no words in it. lines.speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lilmoth.fish-trader-house
lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: Salts-The-Catch. Fish is my trade, and this is my house. I ask nothing of whoever comes through the door. Nesh-Deeka waits at the far end of the room.

lines.speaker: npc.nesh-deeka
lines.text: You are back, my hand. I still cannot say what the Hist at Low-Reed Village has done.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.text: My lockbox is empty. I hope whoever has the jar finds who cut my tree.

lines.speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
lines.prompt: Then I will take it.
lines.text: Then try. The lockbox is locked, and its key stays on me. If you take the jar, you take all I have left of my tree.
